- When sentiment is high (≥0.77) and forecast peaks sharply, reduce peak values by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.27) and forecast is rising, apply downward bias of 2–5% to reflect mean reversion.
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 3–8% in the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27/0.80), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after a high forecast, model often lags — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by 2–4% downward.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period — reduce first 5–7 days by 3–6% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to overpredict — apply 5–10% downward correction to all values.
